newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called steady after Tues. slide.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called steady after Tues. slide.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open flat to higher Wednesday after yesterday's losses due to liquidation of long positions.
Brokers and traders said the power complex is showing signs of stablizing although fundamental factors such as weather and rising supply remained bearish.
"Fundamentals are weak. There's no news to support the market right now," said a West Coast electricity dealer.

In over-the-counter business, July Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $26.75-27.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Tuesday's settlement at $26.82, while July California-Oregon Border (COB) at $16.90-17.00 against yesterday's $16.76.
While parts of the Southwest are experiencing triple digit heat, rise in air-conditioning demand has been also offset by generation capacity coming back spring maintenance outages.
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at Palo Verde nuclear stationin Arizona as expected returned to 100 percent power early Wednesday. The unit was curtailed Monday to repair a feedwater heater tube leak.
A 150 MW hydro turbine, operated by Seattle City and Light Co, was heard shut for a brief outage.

In the latest six to 10 day forecasts, temperatures in the Northwest would average near to slightly above normal with above normal temperatures, while readings in the Southwest would run near normal over most of the region but below normal in the far western area.
